answer: The orchard multiplier is published, charged in wander, and nadir lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 14 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 3003 identities would post 602 proofs and burn roughly 24 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
